title: Whether the object of saving faith is remission of sins already obtained, or remission to be obtained
pass_a_gloss: Article XX. Whether the object of saving faith is remission of sins already obtained, or remission of sins to be obtained and secured — where incidentally Bellarmine's chief argument against the object and nature of justifying faith is solved. 1. The question is whether the object of justifying faith is remission already had, or rather Christ and the promise of remission to be obtained through faith. 2. We with the Orthodox: the primary object of justifying faith is Christ the Mediator, and God's promise in him; faith justifies not because it believes remission already formally inheres, but because it apprehends Christ, in whom remission is offered and through faith applied. 3. Bellarmine's argument — if faith were trust of particular remission already had, it would presuppose the justification it is said to cause — is solved: faith does not presuppose remission as already inhering before faith, but follows and applies it; the object is the promise and Christ, not remission as a prior possession.
pass_b_english: Article XX. Whether the object of saving faith is remission of sins already obtained, or remission to be obtained.
1. Is justifying faith's object remission already had, or Christ and the promise of remission through faith?

2. With the Orthodox: the primary object is Christ the Mediator and God's promise in him. Faith justifies not by believing remission already formally inheres, but by apprehending Christ, in whom remission is offered and by faith applied.

3. Bellarmine: if faith were trust of particular remission already had, it would presuppose the justification it causes. Solved: faith does not presuppose remission as inhering before faith; it follows and applies it. The object is the promise and Christ — not remission as prior possession.
source_text:
ART. XX.
Utrum objectum fidei salvificae sit remissio peccatorum jam impetrata? An vero sit remissio peccatorum impetranda & obtinenda: Ubi obiter solvitur praecipuum argumentum Bellarmini, contra objectum & naturam fidei justificantis.

1. Quaeritur an objectum fidei justificantis sit remissio jam habita, an potius CHRISTUS & promissio remissionis obtinendae per fidem.

2. Nos cum Orthodoxis: objectum fidei justificantis primarium est CHRISTUS Mediator, & DEI promissio in ipso; fides justificat non quia credit remissionem jam formaliter inesse, sed quia CHRISTUM apprehendit, in quo remissio offertur & per fidem applicatur.

3. Bellarmini argumentum — si fides esset fiducia remissionis particularis jam habitae, praesupponeret justificationem quam dicitur causare — solvitur: fides non praesupponit remissionem tanquam jam inhaerentem ante fidem, sed eam consequitur & applicat; objectum est promissio & CHRISTUS, non remissio tanquam praevia possessio.
